_readme: The reference set behind Landlord Navigator's deterministic checks.
WHAT IS IN HERE, AND WHY IT IS NARROW. Every entry records one thing only:
whether a jurisdiction runs a named programme a residential landlord has to
be enrolled in, and which office administers it. That is deliberate. The
existence of Seattle's RRIO or Philadelphia's rental licence is a stable,
long-standing, widely documented fact. The fee, the renewal month and the
ordinance number are none of those things — they change, they vary by unit
count, and a wrong one printed as fact is worse for a landlord than no
answer at all. So no fee, no date and no citation appears anywhere in this
file, and the engine is built so it never needs one: every finding ends by
naming the office to confirm with.
CONFIDENCE. Each claim carries "high" or "check". "high" means the
programme is well established and the finding is written as a statement.
"check" means it is likely but the landlord should confirm before acting,
and the finding says so in those words. A jurisdiction absent from this file
produces a coverage finding that names the gap rather than silence — see
the not-covered branch in api/_lib/landlord-audit.js.
MAINTENANCE. This was compiled from general knowledge on the date below and
has not been reconciled line by line against each authority's current
published rules. Treat review_by as a real deadline: an entry that is a year
stale should either be re-checked or removed. Adding a jurisdiction is the
single highest-value change anyone can make to this product.

lead_disclosure.applies_to: Residential housing built before 1978, with narrow exemptions such as housing for the elderly or disabled with no child resident, and leases of 100 days or fewer.
lead_disclosure.obligation: Before a lease is signed, the landlord must give the tenant the EPA-approved lead hazard information pamphlet, disclose any known lead-based paint or hazards and any records or reports they hold, and include a signed lead warning statement in the lease. The signed disclosure has to be kept for three years.
lead_disclosure.why_it_matters: This one is federal, so it applies in every state, and it is the obligation small landlords most often have no record of having met. A missing signed disclosure is a documentation failure that is entirely within the landlord's own control to fix at the next lease.
lead_disclosure.authority: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, administered locally through your state or city housing authority

registration.programme: Residential rental property registration with the county assessor
registration.authority: the county assessor for the county the property sits in

registration.programme: Landlord registration
registration.authority: your municipal clerk, or the New Jersey Bureau of Housing Inspection for larger buildings

lead.programme: Periodic lead-based paint inspection of pre-1978 rental units
lead.authority: your municipality's lead inspection or code enforcement office
the Massachusetts Childhood Lead Poisoning Prevention Program at the Department of Public Health
lead.what_it_adds: Massachusetts does not stop at disclosure. Where a child under six lives in a pre-1978 unit, the owner is required to have lead hazards removed or covered, and the duty sits with the owner whether or not they knew about the paint.

lead.programme: Maryland's lead rental certification programme for pre-1978 rental housing
lead.authority: the Maryland Department of the Environment
lead.what_it_adds: Maryland requires affected pre-1978 rental units to be registered and to hold a current lead inspection certificate, which is a step beyond the federal disclosure.

lead.programme: Rhode Island's lead certificate requirement for pre-1978 rental units
lead.authority: the Rhode Island Department of Health
lead.what_it_adds: Rhode Island requires a certificate showing the unit has been inspected for lead hazards, over and above the federal disclosure.

deposit.authority: the New York State Attorney General's Office
the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
deposit.note: Florida gives landlords a choice between holding the deposit in a separate account and posting a surety bond, but keeping it in a personal account is not one of the options.

registration.note: Chicago does not run a general rental registry the way Seattle or Minneapolis do, so there is usually nothing to register. The obligations that catch landlords here are in the Residential Landlord and Tenant Ordinance instead.

lease_attachment.document: the city's summary of the Residential Landlord and Tenant Ordinance, which has to be attached to every lease and to every renewal

deposit_rules.note: The RLTO sets its own rules for how a security deposit is held, receipted and returned, and the penalties for getting it wrong are among the stiffest in the country.

registration.note: Austin has no general rental registration for ordinary landlords — its registration programme applies to properties that have accumulated code violations.

registration.note: Most Florida municipalities require a business tax receipt of residential landlords; Florida itself runs no statewide rental registry.
